text: The islands are hot and humid; the region's fixed weather is a steady sea wind and warm rain.
Risky in the interior: bandits in the burnt forts, predators in the dens, slaughterfish in the shallows at the coast.
Mangrove coasts, paddy fauna, wading birds, guar and crabs fill the islands.
The people of the islands live on rice, fish, salvage and ferrying; Lilmoth is the market for all of it.
Lilmoth's second Hist, grown in 4E 8 and cut off from the others, is the islands' feared tree; the Three Waters keep their own pool.

The Lilmothiit withdrew inland over generations and the Knahaten Flu (2E 560-603) finished their remnant. The Empire's forts and road came later and were left at the secession (4E 5-10). The planters' estates had emptied in the Third Era. Lilmoth was destroyed in 4E 48, and the islands were refilled in the generations after.
Low and flat with a few low hills, cut by inlets and inner channels; roads link the towns across land and ferries.
Green rice paddies, stilt villages and brick ruins in vines, with sea on every side.
A group of islands that holds Lilmoth, the estates of the rebuilt coast and an Imperial road gone to ruin.
Lilmoth-coast Argonians, tenants and labourers on the estates, garrison families of the Warden forts and the Three Waters Tribe.
Lilmoth leads the islands; Archwarden forts hold the east and the south-west, some of them against Lilmoth's wishes; Uluo's Three Waters people hold the north.
The island is breezy. Salt spray and sea mist blow in off Topal Bay.
Pirates, smugglers and the sea itself threaten visitors to the island.
Scrub covers the hills, with gulls, crabs and kelp beds along the shore.
The island lives on customs levies, smuggling and salvage in Topal Bay.
Sailors' charms and a small Nine shrine at the belvedere serve the island's few people.
An Imperial retreat island; the signal tower and belvedere were built to watch the bay.
A low hilly island with rocky shores and a high spine running through it.
Low grey hills, scrub, white-washed lookout and a rocky shore.
An island west of Gideon holding the Archwardens' lookout and a smugglers' cache.
A handful of watchers and smugglers live on the island, the watchers at the belvedere and the smugglers at the cave.
The Archwardens' customs watch holds the belvedere and the smugglers hold the cave.
Hot and wet: rain and fog are the commonest weathers, with clear spells that come and go by chance.
Risky away from roads and dangerous at the Velothi ruins. The Thorn road and the towns are mostly safe.
Jungle hardwood, tree-ferns, vines and bright fungus; mudcrabs and slaughterfish along the banks and in the inlet, giant snakes and giant spiders inland, grass and saltrice near Thorn.
Timber, quarried stone, hides and sap, sold to Thorn; saltrice and tools come back.
The sky-blue people hold their city's Hist to be asleep; hamlets keep cairns for it, while the Root-Folk keep their own trees.

Barsaebic Ayleids and Cantemiric Velothi settled the country around Arnesia, Archon and Thorn before their extinction. The Arnesian War of 3E 396 began as a slave revolt in southern Dres lands and ended with Morrowind annexing Arnesia; from 3E 432 the Argonians began to reclaim the ground, and slavers were still active in Arnesia in the late Third Era.
A long inlet from the bay runs west to Tsonac, with rivers branching off to the south and north-west; rises of 30 to 60 m stand between them, and the ground is marshy at the shore.
Terraced stone towns among tall hardwoods, a broad bay inlet with muddy banks, Velothi ruins under vines.
The Arnesian Jungle takes its name from Arnesia, the east-coast country around Thorn and Archon, a settlement and region near both cities.
Mostly Stone-Sleeper Argonians, with Root-Folk hunters, Warden garrisons and field-owners' crews near Thorn and Dunmer traders on the road.
In 4E 201 the jungle is the Stone-Sleepers' home country, with Tsonac as capital and the Warden forts, camps and posts stand round Thorn at its coastal edge.
Breezy and a little drier than the forest, with morning mist and rain the commonest weathers.
Naga and Paatru raiders, giant snakes, falls on the summit paths and cold wind at night on the open top.
Grass, scrub, stunted trees and lizards; giant snakes and wild marsh-lizards; fewer insects than the forest.
Penned marsh-lizards, hides, hunting and tin chimes traded with the Paatru and with Korydon and taken to Helstrom at the Root Talk.
Sithis and the Hist among the Chime-Keepers; watchfires on the peaks are a small offering to the Hist.
No stake tells of the ridge's past. The Kothringi-named hamlets on it, Nacydes and Tydeos, are read as Kothringi places resettled by Argonians after 2E 560 because the ridge is dry.
A long spine of firm ground rising from marsh, with rock outcrops, two summits, steep faces on the north and shelving slopes on the south.
Rock outcrops and grass-scrub above the reeds, stone-footed huts, windchimes, watchfires at night and wide views over the marsh.
Aunike Ridge is a ridge of firm ground west and south-west of Helstrom, with two peaks and two Chime-Keeper hamlets.
Chime-Keepers at Nacydes and Tydeos; Paatru and Naga hold the camps at its margin.
In 4E 201 its hamlets keep watch from the peaks and trade chimes for hides with the Paatru camp to the west; Naga bands of Salt-Tooth Camp range across it.
The basin is hot and humid, with heavy rain and steam rising off the water after it.
Hostile posts, swamp predators and haunted ruins make the basin dangerous.
Reeds and mangrove grow in the basin, with gar, mudcrabs and hackwings.
Fishing, salvaged mine metal, tolls on Soulrest's Argonians and a little timber.
Sithis, the nearest Hist to Soulrest and burned-mine shrines.
Imperial mines and timber concessions here were destroyed by the tribes in 3E 427; the Mine-Burners have held it since.
A shallow basin of channels and islets, with dark water between them.
Flooded channels, scorched timber and tiered stilt halls mark the basin.
A flooded basin of channels and islets with Jarecai and Kharaxos as its towns.
Mine-Burner Argonians, Chime-Keepers, Root-Folk outposts and Paatru hunters; about 100 people.
Jarecai's council rules; Soulrest depends on the basin's Hist for hatching and burial; the Chime-Keepers hold Oeneas.
The air is humid and the rain frequent. Black tidal water fills the western river mouths, brackish and slow.
The ruins and the marsh between them are dangerous, while the roads are far safer.
Lamias live in Loriasel's caverns, and giant snakes, wamasu and hackwings range the plain.
The region lives on reed, fish, tolls and scavenging in the Ayleid ruins.
The Hist pool at Jal-Veesa is the living shrine of the region, while the Ayleid shrines lie in ruin.
Barsaebic Ayleids were driven east after 1E 198 and occupied north-eastern Black Marsh and parts of Blackwood, founding Silyanorn, Twyllbek, Archon, Thorn, Loriasel and Gandranen.
A hummocky plain west of Stormhold, with ruins standing on mounds and hills.
White Ayleid stone in reed beds; stilt huts and weirs; a long road west.
Barsaebica is named for the Barsaebic Ayleids and holds Loriasel, Gandranen, Gemin and the western road to Slough Point.
Veesa-Teeleel reed-wardens, Naga bands and the Lukiul of Slough Point.
A country of ruins, weirs and one frontier village; the Veesa-Teeleel guard the ruins as sick ground.
Warm shallows over cold deep water; the surface under a fixed grey overcast and a steady swell.
Dangerous across the floor and deadly at Echo Deep and the outer spires: dreugh, slaughterfish and deep water where a diver's breath runs out.
Kelp, coral, slaughterfish, dreugh, glowgill guar at the western edge.
The spires yield salvage: drowned metal, carved stone and coral-crusted glass. The steward at Bell Station decides who dives.
Argonians hold the deep as the abode of the drowned and pray before diving.
Myth says the Southern Sea swallowed Murkmire in the Dawn Era, when the Hist's land sank but for one corner; the spires are what is told to remain.
A shelf of silt about forty metres down, spires to eight metres below the surface and a trench.
Blue-green water over silt, coral and kelp, spires standing from the floor, a black trench.
The sea east of Lilmoth covers drowned ground with spires and a trench.
The sea floor has no residents. Divers and dreugh come here.
Bell Station's licensed divers salvage the spires; elsewhere the sea floor is unclaimed.
The air is humid. Long rains and fog lie over the bogs; the frontier roads are mud where they are not causeway.
Sul-Xan raiders, giant spiders and hackwings make the frontier dangerous away from the roads.
Giant spiders, hackwings, hackwings and crocodiles live in the hills and bogs.
Fish, clay, hunting, herbs and trade along the Blackwood Road support the frontier's people.
Dibella and Z'en remembered; Hist shoots; the Sul-Xan's Dagon heresy.
Kothringi homeland in large numbers; the Knahaten Flu emptied it by 2E 603; the Maran mission died at Umpholo in the 3E.
Flooded hillscape with steep, lightly forested hills at the western frontier of Black Marsh.
A flooded hillscape of bog and cairn-fields, with steep hills rising from standing water.
Blackwood here is the far south-west of the province, the Argonian side of Blackwood.
Lukiul, Naka-Desh and Hutan-Tzel, with Nibenese-descended families.
Dead towns, a few river villages and Hutan-Tzel outposts; Sul-Xan raiders are feared.
Humid and warm; sea mist on the south coast; rain is frequent and the low creeks stand full.
Highwaymen, burn-gas, flooded mines and hostile tribes; roads and towns are safer.
Red gum, mangrove, wading birds, sea-drakes at the shore; the burn-scar is bare.
Timber, stone, fish and salt for Soulrest; the mines are derelict.
Sithis and the Hist through inland trees; a few Nine shrines of Imperial families.
Gold and timber concessions ran here until the tribes burned them in 3E 427; the Great Burn's underground network reached the cape in 1E 2828.
Low hills up to about 45 m behind the coast, flat sandy shores, salt creeks and mangrove edges.
Red-gum hills, black burn-scars, grey-stone Imperial ruins and stilt villages on the coast.
The cape is the peninsula behind Soulrest. It holds the old Imperial mines and timber concessions, a few villages and a burn scar.
Umber coast folk: Argonians, Khajiit coasters and Imperial-descended families, with Banujha watchers and a Naka-Desh river station at the edges.
Villages and licensed camps work timber and stone under Soulrest's council; the mines stand derelict; Banujha mine-burners keep watch posts at its edges.
Drier than the jungle; the mesa tops hold little water and cold nights follow hot days.
Dangerous away from roads: Sarpa raiders, Velothi undead and cliff falls.
Scrub, tall grass and thorn-bush on the tops; crocodiles, giant snakes, hawks and giant spiders in the gorges and the Sarpa on the western edge.
Chixathe Mesa yields quarried stone, chalk and lime, hides and books, sent off the mesa to Thorn and the river towns.
A mix of Hist customs: the Sarpa keep their own tree beyond the edge, the Stone-Sleepers raise cairns for Tsonac's sleeping Hist and the Agaceph read their mission books at hatchings.
The Cantemiric Velothi settled the east of Black Marsh before the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560-603 killed them; their ruins at Kaochalit, Balormaak and Vorannuhl stand on the mesa.
Flat mesa tops 60 to 110 m above the lowland, cliffs on the edges and river gorges between them.
Pale cliffs and flat tops, white chalk dust, stone cuts, rivers in green gorges.
Chixathe Mesa lies between the Arnesian country and the Middle Argonian interior.
No single culture: Stone-Sleepers, Root-Folk, Agaceph, Sedge-Wardens and Clay-Mound families, with Sarpa to the west.

In 4E 201 it is a thin, mixed country: Stone-Sleeper hamlets and quarries to the north and east, Warden fort at Chalkmoth, Root-Folk and Sedge-Warden outposts, an Agaceph hamlet in the south and Sarpa on the western edge.
Milder than the interior, with fog and frequent rain.
Smuggler landings, mudcrabs, giant snakes and ghosts in the three ruins; the inland margin has Sarpa raiders.
Marsh grasses, reeds and salt-tolerant shrubs; crabs, eels, hackwings and coastal crocodiles; temperate grassland more than swamp, as in the rest of the north.
Salt, stone, timber, clay and pottery, sold up and down the coast to Thorn and Archon. The wardens' posts take a share in tolls, and smugglers take another at the landings.
Mostly Hist-less: coast villages send eggs inland; Velothi ancestor tablets mark the ruins; the Sarpa read the wind.

Cantemiric Velothi held this coast from Thorn to Archon until the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 killed them. Dres slave-ships sailed from Thorn across it; the Arnesian War of 3E 396 was fought on its northern margin.
A flat to gently rolling plain behind a wide bay, cut by shallow rivers that end in mud-flats at the coast. Low clay rises carry the villages; headlands of dark stone hold the ruins.
A pale shore of grey mud-flats and sandy points with grass behind, bright green after rain, low red clay rises, black Velothi ruins on the headlands, sea fog.
The bight is the sea-bay that lies between Thorn in the north and the Arorha shore in the south, with a belt of grassland behind it.
A mix of the clay-mound people of Arorha, the Stone-Sleepers of Tsonac at Ysan, a Root-Folk watch at Yuva-Goli, Warden Marches families at the posts and a Sarpa camp inland.

A thinly peopled coast: Arorha at its south end, small hamlets of Tsonac's stone-folk and Helstrom's Root-Folk, Warden posts toward Thorn and three dead Velothi ruins. The coast road from Thorn to Seafalls and Archon runs through it.
Hot and humid, with frequent heavy rain and fog off the estuary at dawn.
Hackwings, crocodiles and haunted Kothringi and Imperial ruins; the north is wilder than the road.
Mangrove, reed and fern; hackwings, eels and crows over the mud; gar in the channels.
Hunting, herbs, red-clay pottery, fishing and the Leyawiin trade along the Blackwood Road.
Dibella in Gideon, Sithis in the villages; Kothringi chimes in the ruins; the Hist is a planted cutting.

Barsaebic Ayleids, Kothringi and Imperial settlers each built here. The Kothringi died in the Knahaten Flu, and the Imperial garrisons left at the secession; Gideon alone kept the Imperial courthouse.
Mudflats and mangrove channels with a few raised banks; the Onkobra delta lays down red clay and the estuary's low ground stands under water.
Black water between stilt houses, red mud, tangled mangrove roots and grey Imperial stone along the road.
A low coastal delta of mangrove channels around Gideon, the province's western gateway. Gideon, its villages and its roads sit on the few dry rises.
Majority Lukiul Argonians, Nibenese-descended families, Naka-Desh river-folk and a few Khajiit sailors. Perhaps 130 live in the region.
Gideon's council holds the dry land and the Archwardens hold Fort Silvermoth on the south road. The rest is mangrove, and it is crossed only by the Blackwood Way and the delta channels.
Warm and humid, with rain squalls over the open water and fog on the shores the commonest weathers.
Slaughterfish in the deep water, boat-robbers and smugglers; the Gysilla toll and Truowa's quarrels are the social hazards.
Eels, reed fish, crocodiles in the delta, water-birds in the reed beds and rice paddies on raised banks.
Fish, eels, saltrice, pottery, sap and a through trade in cloth, tin and salt, with tolls taken at Gysilla and Truowa.
The Hist at each village tree; Sithis privately; shrines of the Nine kept by foreign factors at Truowa and a few Archein households.
No song or stake tells of the lake before the Empire. The interior rivers pool here, which made it a meeting place for trade long before the Empire built a post at Gysilla.
A shallow basin with flat shores, silt islets and a delta of river arms at the north-west; the south shore is firmer.
A wide pale-grey lake fringed with reed, silt islets with lantern posts, stilt quays on the south-east shore and stone-footed farmhouses on the northern deltas.
Lake Ulaish is the large lake south-east of Helstrom where the river arms of the interior spread out and slow before moving on.

A mix: the Root-Folk's islet stations, stone-footed farm hamlets in the Stormhold manner, clay-mound people at Marzai, Tumnatu fishers, the Archein garrison at Gysilla and Truowa's Lilmoth-linked merchants.

In 4E 201 the lake carries the boat traffic between Helstrom, Aroxhu, Truowa and the waters toward Korydon and Blackrose. Archein families toll it from Fort Gysilla in the Archwardens' name; Truowa's merchants and the Aroxhu mound people compete for its trade.
Hot, wet and still, with heavy rain and morning fog the commonest weathers and clear days rare.
Medusas in the deep wood, Naga ambushes on the river arms, Paatru who kill on sight and the moving wood itself, which can swallow a path overnight.
Great Hist trees, mosses and ferns; fellrunners, medusas, rootworms, crocodiles, flesh-flies and torchbugs. Fellrunner pale down is the region's famous good.
Fellrunner feathers, sap, eggs, hides and river fish; farmers trade sacks of feathers to hunters, and a single armband of the pale down lets a hunter move through Murkwood undetected.
The Hist: every settlement sends its people to a village tree to hatch and bury. The Root Talk at Helstrom is the occasion on which the tribes hear the Hist through the tree-minders.

In the Imperial Simulacrum of 3E 399 Jagar Tharn hid a piece of the Staff of Chaos in Murkwood, and the Eternal Champion fetched it. The forest has moved many times since; Helstrom and the Root-Folk have stood beside it through all of them.
Low, wet ground cut by braided river arms flowing toward the lake, with dry rises where the roots hold the soil. Heart-Mud flats lie on the south.
A dark wood of huge roots, hanging moss and black water; light comes green and dim, the air is thick and loud with insects and the forest never looks the same twice.

Murkwood is the legendary dark forest said to move, on a river deep in the swamps of Black Marsh and home to many medusas. The Conclave of Baal at Stormhold claims to find where it stands by reading the Elder Scrolls with an ancient tablet; in 4E 201 it stands around Helstrom.
The Root-Folk of Helstrom (Saxhleel) hold the heart; the Hutan-Tzel hold the west; tribeless Naga and the toad-like Paatru hold the camps at the margin.
In 4E 201 the forest crowds the river arms around Helstrom, held by the Root-Folk, the Hutan-Tzel at its west edge and several camps of Naga and Paatru. Few outsiders come.
The country is hot and humid, with heavy rain and low cloud over the channels.
Paatru camps, haunted Kothringi ruins and wild predators threaten travellers away from the stations.
Reeds, ferns, osheeja gar and mudcrabs; hackwings over the banks.
The river-folk live by gar fishing, salt-and-iron barter, herbs and the caravan trade.
Hist roots and chimes in memory of the Kothringi; Dibella wayside shrines.
Kothringi land until the Knahaten Flu, then empty; it became the Gideon-Leyawiin trade route and a river-folk country.
Low river banks and reed flats, drier than the delta, cut by channels.
Reed banks, black rivers, stilt platforms and grey ruin stones.
A region of river forks and low banks between Gideon and the interior, held by Naka-Desh river-folk and a handful of traders.
Naka-Desh river-folk, Lukiul traders and Paatru hunters; about 60 people.
Gul-Tej holds the road; the Naka-Desh keep their stations; Paatru camps hunt the west edge.
Hot and humid all year; the region's fixed weather is heavy warm rain and low mist over the water.
Risky away from the road: slaughterfish in every deep channel, crocodilians on the hummocks, smugglers and swamp disease.
Reed, mangrove, saltrice, slaughterfish, wading birds and mud-crabs.
Rice, fish, reed, shellfish and back-water freight that avoids customs; Archon is the market.
Sithis and the Hist, with the town of Uluo keeping the nearest tree for hatching.

The bayou was Lilmothiit and Cantemiric Velothi ground; no Lilmothiit or Velothi lives here after the Knahaten Flu (2E 560-603), while the Three Waters Tribe survived and spread. Its villages lie east of the island path through Murkmire that Umbriel laid waste in 4E 48.
Flat and braided: channels split and rejoin around thin ridges of firm ground, and the walkable ground is a chain of hummocks joined by raft-bridges. The north climbs slightly to clay mounds.
Sheets of brown water between reed banks and hummocks of trees, lines of raft-houses and herons.
The marsh country between Archon, the Althii islands and the mound country, laced by channels and settled by the Three Waters Tribe. It links Archon with the Lilmoth coast by water.
The people are the Three Waters Argonians. Clay-Mound families live at Badal and Lilmoth-coast families at Oju. Archon's boatmen also work the channels.
The Three Waters Tribe holds the channels and its hamlets, Archon and Lilmoth trade through it and Fort Swiftmoth beside the road has stood empty since the secession.
Hot, humid and rainy; rain falls often and the mounds stand dry above the marsh.
Crocodiles, giant snakes, Sarpa raiders, smuggler landings and ghosts in the Velothi ruins.
Reeds, rice, madder and ochre-stained marsh plants; crocodiles, eels, giant snakes and hackwings; guar on the meadows.
Clay, pottery, dye and ochre; fish and rice; books and illusion-work from the Agaceph; Seafalls' piloting and portage. The river trade to Archon and Thorn runs on clay.
The Aroxhu Hist at the centre; the Spray-Folk's sea-memory; the Agaceph's detachment; Velothi ancestor tablets in the ruins; Sarpa wind-omens.

A tribal country long before the Empire; the East Empire Company's boats worked its clay, and Cantemiric Velothi once held its coast. Since the secession the clay-mound people have been the dominant power.
Low red clay mounds above flat marsh, big lakes in the west and a maze of creeks in the south-east, ending in cliffs and a falls at the coast.
Red-brown mounds in green-grey marsh, bright reed thatch, kilns smoking, pale lakes and brown creeks, black Velothi ruins, white falls at Seafalls.
A broad region of red-clay mounds, lakes and creeks in the east of Middle Argonia, where the Agaceph live.
Oxhu-Teeleel clay-mound people (the bulk), Agaceph raft-folk at Yulca, Icalca, Xibcan and Yina, Spray-Folk at Seafalls, Sarpa camps, a Root-Folk outpost.
The confederacy at Aroxhu is the largest tribal polity of the east; the Agaceph at Yulca and the Spray-Folk at Seafalls are its neighbours; Skeith's outlaws harass the coast.
Overcast and rainy with sea-mist, bright on clear days.
Pirates, dreugh, slaughterfish and drowned dead in the wrecks; deep water beyond the shelf, far from any shore.
Kelp, fish shoals, eels, crabs and dreugh; sea-birds along the shore.
Fishing, piloting, salvage, piracy and smuggling; the north-east link between Thorn, Seafalls and Archon is run by sea as well as by road.
The Spray-Folk hold that memories the Hist let fall are kept in the sea; sailors leave knotted cords and painted shells on shore for the lost.

In the Dawn Era the Ehlnofey war sank most of the Hist's domain into the Padomaic, 'leaving only a small corner left standing', later Black Marsh. Topal the Pilot charted it first. Uriel Septim V's fleet sailed across it against Akavir in 3E 288.
A shallow shelf that falls to deep water within a few miles of the shore; sandbanks and shoals off the Seafalls point and Skeith Isle.
Grey-green water with long swell, white surf on the shore, dark kelp beds and pale sandbanks, drowned timbers rising from the shelf.

The Padomaic is the vast ocean around most of Tamriel; here it is the eastern edge of Black Marsh, with Archon and Thornmarsh on its shore. The region covers only the shelf and open water off Thorn, Hatandros Bight and Skeith Isle.
Sea people: pilots and fishers of Seafalls and Archon, chartered pirate crews from Marque Landing, smuggler boats from Hollow Tide Camp, Dunmer traders from Tear.

Argonia has no navy. Chartered pirates do that work. Boats from Archon, Seafalls and Thorn work the shelf; the Archwardens' writ ends at the quay. The wrecks of a Dunmer slaver, a smuggler's sloop, an Imperial man-of-war and a freighter lie here.
The Sea of Mists is warm and humid with mist most mornings; rain and thunderstorms are common.
Sea-drakes, shoals, pirates and sudden fog threaten every boat that leaves the shore.
Sea-drakes, fat sleeper, longlure eelfin, spotted seatrout, seabirds.
The sea's coast lives on fishing, wreck salvage, coastal freight and smuggling in small boats.
Sailors hold rites for the drowned, and Argonian boats carry a Sithis token on the stem.
Pirates of the Southern Sea avoid attention. Many of its seafarers are Khajiit. Legend says Murkmire once extended further south and was swallowed by the sea.
The sea is a shelf about 35 m deep, scattered with sandbars and low islets.
Grey-green water, mist banks, low islets and mangrove edges.
The Sea of Mists is the part of the Southern Sea south of Cape Percar, a grey-green shelf sea off Black Marsh's south coast.
Argonian fishers, Khajiit coasters and a few Bosmer seafarers work the sea's boats and landings along the coast.
Fishing boats and small coasters ply it, with salvagers at the wrecks and smugglers' landings.
Windy, salt-laden and drier than the mainland, with sea-fog and rain.
Outlaws, trapped coves, cliffs and nesting hackwings; the surf off the shingle is rough.
Sea-grass, scrub, goats gone feral, sea-birds, crabs and eels; no Hist and little soil.
Piracy, smuggling and salvage; the island has little soil and imports food from the mainland.
Ships' figureheads and sea-luck; the Imperial shrine in the keep is stacked with crates.
The Empire's coastal keep was built to watch the pirate trade of the Archon coast; at the secession the garrison left and pirates took the island.
A single rise of dark rock with cliff edges to the west and north, shingle beaches to the south and east, a central crag.
Dark grey-green rock in sea-worn crags, thin grass, wind-bent scrub, grey shingle beaches, a keep on a rise and a spire called the Grey Tooth.
A rocky island east of the mainland, home to two outlaw camps, an old Imperial keep and a single crag. Its dark green-grey rock matches the round island off Arnesia's coast.
About forty outlaws of mixed origin: Argonian boat-crews, Dunmer from Tear, runaway Archein families, Khajiit dealers.
Two rival outlaw crews hold it: the half-chartered pirates at Marque Landing and the smugglers at Hollow Tide Camp. Mainland boats avoid it.
The bay is warm. Sea breezes, sea fog and passing rain storms come over it.
Pirates, reefs and old wrecks threaten boats on the eastern coast of the bay and slaughterfish crowd the reef water.
Sharks, crabs, mullet, eels and sea-birds live in the bay's shallow waters.
The bay's people live by fishing, shipping, smuggling and salvage along its shores.
Sailors keep charms and make offerings to the Nine and to Sithis on the bay.
The Imperial fleet policed the bay until the secession; Red Bramman's pirates used its mangrove river in the First Era.
A shallow bay with a mangrove shoreline over sand and mud flats.
The bay shows grey-green water, a mangrove coast and sandbars along its shores.
The bay enclosed by Elsweyr, Black Marsh and Cyrodiil, with Soulrest on its eastern shore.
Seafarers, many of them Khajiit, plus Argonian fishers and Bosmer pilots.
Piracy continues on the eastern coast; the Archwardens have no navy and Soulrest's merchants hire their own boats.
The washes are hot, humid and still; rain falls most days and the water stands across the whole lowland between the cape and the delta.
Crocodilians, gar, deep channels, bandits and the Rose; the deep washes are dangerous.
Reeds, mangroves, cypress, gar, crocodilians, herons; sea-drakes at the south shore.
Tolls at the confluence, fish, reeds, rice, chimes, smuggling.
Drowned Hist at Blackrose, Sithis and a regard for Z'en and Dibella at Toklea.
Lilmothiit lands, then Kothringi towns, then the Imperial prison and city; Murkmire lies to the south-east.
Dead-flat lowland of standing water with tiny rises; channels braid round low islands of reed and mud.
Brown water, reed beds, stilt towns, boardwalks, drowned domes and mist.
The washes are the wet country around Blackrose where three rivers converge; Bramman's river runs out to Topal Bay.
Olive lake-folk, oxblood Chime-Keepers, rose delta farmers, umber carters, the Blackguards' heirs and Naga.
Blackrose city holds the lake; the Rose is held by the Blackguards' heirs; oxblood towns, rose delta villages and umber road towns sit around them.
Hot and heavy, with rain and a warm fog on the channels the commonest weathers.
Dragon's-tongue patches that kill the careless, deep-water predators, Tumnatu parties and fog-bound channels in which boats lose their way.
Dragon's-tongue, cattails, reed, water-lilies; eels, crocodiles, marsh-lizards and swarms of flesh-flies.
Dragon's-tongue and other swamp herbs, chimes, rope and boats from Korydon, fish and pelts traded north to Helstrom and south to Blackrose.
Sithis and the Hist; Korydon adds Z'en, kept at a chime-hung shrine.
No song survives of this swamp's past. Its Kothringi-named towns, Korydon, Myroleon and Nemeon, are read as old Kothringi places that Argonians resettled after the Knahaten Flu (2E 560–603).
Flat and low, cut by many channels, with ring-like firm ground such as the one under Korydon; the south opens into the larger waters toward Blackrose.
The swamp is a grey-green maze of cattails, reed and black water, with rings of dry ground and stilt towns hung with metal chimes.

The Ultherus Swamp, also called Utherus, is a region of Black Marsh of which little is known; the beautiful but deadly dragon's-tongue plant is especially common there. It lies south of Helstrom around Korydon.
The Chime-Keepers of Korydon, Nemeon and Myroleon, Tumnatu hunters and a few Root-Folk boatmen.
In 4E 201 the swamp is crossed by boat; Korydon's Chime-Keepers harvest the dragon's-tongue, Tumnatu hunters keep to the reeds and a Root-Folk waystation sits at its south.
Humid and warm, with heavy rain and thunder in the region's weather; the lower causeway stretches lie under shallow water that carts wade.
Risky away from the roads: crocodiles, Naga bands and the haunted ruins. The northern road is mostly safe.
Crocodiles in the ravines, hackwings, giant snakes and wamasu in the deeper water.
River and road trade with Morrowind and Alten Corimont, saltrice, crystals and reed.
The town-square Hist, the grave-stake tradition and Dunmer ancestor stones.
Barsaebic Ayleids built Silyanorn here; the Dunmer made the area the foothold of their slave trade; the Pact made Stormhold its capital; Umbriel overran it in 4E 48 with light damage.
Stormhold stands on a mountainside and ravine-cut mounds; the rest is rolling marsh plain rising to the Morrowind border.
Stone-footed farmsteads and mounds linked by stone causeways, the river and its branches and the grey Imperial forts.
The valley of storms holds Stormhold, the northern gate, with its customs, its forts and its farms.
Argonians and the oldest Dunmer minority in the province, with Veesa-Teeleel reed-wardens to the west.
A frontier of causeway farms, Archwarden forts and a Vicecanon-run city, still the province's working border with Morrowind.
